subject: BYOK lightweight wrap-token bridge proposal and network guardrails
body:
From: Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@fintechco.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: secops@fintechco.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on BYOK wrap-token approach for private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our SecOps team reviewed Redwood's BYOK options and asked for a short write-up on the lightweight wrap-token idea you mentioned — specifically:

- How the wrap-token is minted and attested from our HSM (we use an on-prem Thales appliance)
- TTL and rotation cadence for the wrap-token vs. customer-owned KEKs
- Network controls: which subnets/ports need egress to Redwood and whether we can tether the handshake to a VPN peering only
- Evidence we can provide for auditors (key lineage, signing events)

Can you send a short proposal and an initial action list we can include in our procurement packet?

Appreciate it,
Tim
Lead SecOps Engineer
FintechCo

----
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@fintechco.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK wrap-token approach for private deployment

Tim — thanks, and great questions. Attaching a sketched diagram and a short playbook PDF. High level summary below; full answers & checklist attached.

Summary:
- Minting: Customer HSM generates a short-lived wrap-token by wrapping a freshly generated symmetric ephemeral key (EK) under the customer KEK. The EK is used only to encrypt the model-serving key blob during handoff. Wrap-token is an opaque, signed artifact (JWS) containing HKDF-derived metadata and issuance TTL.
- Attestation: The HSM signs the wrap-token with an asymmetric attestation key; Redwood verifies the signature and optionally performs a CHALLENGE/RESPONSE over a mutually authenticated TLS session.
- TTL: Default wrap-token TTL = 15 minutes; recommended maximum 1 hour. KEK rotation policy remains customer-controlled (e.g., monthly/quarterly). We expect wrap-token rotation to be continuous and independent of KEK rotation.
- Network: Minimal egress from the customer VPC to Redwood control plane endpoints (TLS port 443) plus an optional mTLS port (8443) for attestation exchange. We support VPN peering-only setups; no public IPs required for handshakes if peering is established.

Action items attached: 'mvp-operator-playbook.pdf' and 'wrap-token-arch.png'. I[0m can draft a one-page evidence template for auditors.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: BYOK wrap-token — proposed operator flow (internal)

Folks — looping Marcus in (infra) and Olga (security ops) to validate network constraints. My quick sketch of an operator-level flow:

1) Customer operator creates a wrap request and signs it in the HSM; HSM returns wrap-token JWS.
2) Operator POSTs wrap-token to Redwood Private control-plane endpoint over peered VPN (mutual TLS enforced).
3) Redwood validates JWS, optional attestation challenge (nonce exchange); if valid, Redwood provisions an ephemeral serving key encrypted under EK and returns a receipt.
4) Serving nodes request the encrypted key blob from Redwood over internal private network; blob is cached with TTL tied to wrap-token expiry.

Concerns to confirm:
- How we enforce replay protection when we see identical JWS tokens? Need a nonce store or one-time token flagging.
- Whether we can support HSM-sourced asymmetric attestation keys vs customer-managed certs.

Attaching a quick checklist in the drive link.

— Marcus

----
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK wrap-token — proposed operator flow (internal)

All — answered inline:
- Replay protection: we will persist token IDs for the TTL window (15m) in a small LRU store with cryptographic counters; if a token is seen twice we reject the second use. For audit we record token ID, HSM signer cert fingerprint, and the requesting operator identity.
- Attestation modes: support both. For Thales + PKCS#11 HSMs we can consume a signer cert chain; for richer attestation customers can do an attested challenge over TPM/SGX and return attestation quote.
- Network hardening: require peering + mTLS. If customer permits limited outbound to control-plane, fallback to VPN is allowed. No inbound open ports required on customer tenant.

I'll prepare the evidence items: signing event log sample, token ID trace format, and a manifest for the auditor.

Olga
Security Operations Engineer

This addresses most of our concerns. A couple of follow-ups before procurement:

1) Can you confirm the minimum required egress IPs/hostnames (we want to lock to IPs in firewall rules)?
2) For audit: sample entries showing the full key lineage for a single issuance and subsequent rotation would be ideal.
3) If we choose 15m TTL, what are expected operator UX impacts (failures when token expires mid-transfer)?

If you can send answers and the evidence template, we can move to a short MSA addendum and schedule a handoff call with our infra on Monday.

Thanks,
Tim

Subject: Re: BYOK lightweight wrap-token approach for private deployment

Tim — quick answers below and next steps. Full artifacts attached to this thread and in our shared Drive folder.

Answers:
- Egress: three IP ranges used by Redwood control plane for this handoff — 34.210.120.0/24, 52.19.6.0/24, 18.197.32.0/24. We will also publish an mTLS-only FQDN (private) that resolves over the peering link. We can provide signed CRLs/cert thumbprints for your firewall policy team.
- Audit sample: included in 'mvp-operator-playbook.pdf' — shows token ID mapping -> HSM signer cert fingerprint -> issuance timestamp -> redemption event and operator identity.
- Operator UX: 15m TTL is a good default. If a token expires mid-transfer the operator gets a clear 401-style response and the client can transparently retry with a fresh wrap-token. We recommend building an automated retry for short TTLs. For long-running maintenance windows, use a delegated session flow (longer-lived but tied to strict operator identity and IP bounds).

Next steps:
1) We'll push the artifacts to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/BRIDGE-DIAG-2027 (diagram + playbook).
2) Proposal: we prepare a 1-page MSA addendum sketch and an action checklist for your procurement team by Monday EOD.
3) Schedule a 45-minute handoff with FintechCo infra & SRE next Monday 10:00 AM PT — please confirm.
